# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 42 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 42 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_042_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 11, Part 1 — True and False Prophets

**42:1** He showed me men sitting on a bench, and another man sitting in a chair. And he said to me: "Do you see the men sitting on the bench?" "I see them, lord," I said. "These," he said, "are the faithful, and he who sits in the chair is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the servants of God — that is, of the double-minded, not of the faithful."

**42:2** "These double-minded ones come to him as to a diviner and inquire of him what will happen to them. And that false prophet, having no power of the divine Spirit in himself, speaks with them according to their requests and according to the desires of their wicked hearts, and he fills their souls as they wish. For being empty himself, he gives empty answers to empty inquirers. Whatever word is asked of him, he speaks. For he speaks from the emptiness of his own heart. Some word he speaks also by chance correctly, for the devil fills him so that some of his words may come true, so that this prophet may have the more confidence and that the double-minded ones may flock to him the more, and he may lead them astray."

**42:3** "All those therefore who are strong in the faith of the Lord inquire not of him, knowing that there is no truth in him. For no spirit given by God needs to be asked, but having the power of God it speaks by itself, since it speaks as God wills. Therefore when the man who has the divine Spirit comes into an assembly of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and prayer is made by the assembly of those men, then the angel of the prophetic Spirit resting upon him fills the man, and the man, being filled with the Holy Spirit, speaks to the congregation as the Lord wills."

**42:4** "Thus the divine Spirit will be made manifest. Whatever therefore the divine Spirit has power to speak — this power is of the Lord. Therefore hear concerning the Spirit which is from God and from the false spirit, so that you may believe in the true spirit and not trust in the false."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the assembly/ecclesial setting and the Spirit-discernment vocabulary of Hermas.*
